TRANSPARENCY

A useful lens. Never a verdict.

No tool can prove who wrote a text. This one shows its working so you can judge the score for yourself.

How the score is built

The detector measures ten writing-style signals: stock phrasing, sentence rhythm, formulaic openers, personal voice, lists of three, trailing “-ing” clauses, punctuation variety, short sentences, concrete detail and paragraph uniformity. Chat-assistant phrases such as “Sure! Here’s a quick…” count as extra evidence. A weighted combination is mapped to a 0–100 scale. It is a rule-based estimate, not a trained classifier.

Where it goes wrong

Formal, academic or heavily edited human writing can score high. Model output that has been edited by a person can score low. Short passages and languages other than English carry less evidence, so their scores are pulled toward 50 and marked low confidence. Headings and short list items are left out of the sentence statistics.

How rewriting works

When a language model is connected, rewrites are produced by that model and checked so numbers and links are not altered. If the model is unavailable, the tool falls back to offline rules in your browser and tells you.

Do not use this score alone for academic, hiring or disciplinary decisions.

WORTH KNOWING

Questions and answers.

Can it tell for certain that a text was written by AI?

No. The score reflects how closely the writing matches patterns common in model output. It is evidence to weigh, with a stated confidence level, and it is sometimes wrong in both directions.

Is my text uploaded?

Scoring, counting, file reading and offline rewriting all happen in your browser. Only a model-backed rewrite sends your passage to this site’s server and on to the model provider, and the tool tells you when that mode is active.

Why did my own writing get a high score?

Formal and academic writing shares many surface features with model output: even sentence lengths, few contractions and tidy lists. Read the signal list to see which features raised the score. A high score is not evidence that you used AI.

Which languages and files are supported?

Any language can be scored and counted, but the wording signals are tuned for English, so other languages are marked low confidence. You can open .txt, .md and .docx files up to 2 MB and text-based .pdf files up to 10 MB. Scanned PDFs do not contain readable text.

What are the limits?

Scoring and counting accept up to 30,000 characters. Rewriting accepts 3 to 1,500 words and up to 12,000 characters per request, with a limit of 8 model rewrites a minute.

Is it really free?

Yes. Scoring and offline tools cost nothing to run. Model-backed rewriting uses a shared free allowance; when that runs out for the day, the offline rules take over.
